title: Where does the time go when a program sleeps?
question: Sleeping for 30 ms takes 30 ms, but the kernel works for a tiny part of it. What happens in between?
text: Call 1, [clock_nanosleep_time64(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, 0, {0, 30000000}, NULL)](1): [hrtimer_nanosleep](1:hrtimer_nanosleep) Set a high-resolution timer for 30 ms from now. [schedule](1:schedule) Nothing to do until then: give the CPU away. The idle task (swapper) runs, and waits for an interrupt. [hrtimer_wakeup](1:hrtimer_wakeup:any) 30 ms later, the timer's interrupt: wake the sleeper up (it is runnable again).
